theRule.step1: one entry per reason code, the newest of that kind — so fourteen refusals cannot become four lines of the same refusal
theRule.step2: ordered by StoryWeight (3 refusal by memory, 2 what the wave cost it, 1 how it met the wave, 0 routine) and then by recency
theRule.step3: cut to HudText.CreatureStoryLines = 4, then put back in time order, newest first
theRule.fill: routine fills whatever the beats leave over, so a creature nothing has happened to yet still has a full panel
theRule.noTickNeeded: every input is a published field of the snapshot; the ranking is a function of the reason code alone. CreatureStoryTests.Reading_a_creature_s_story_needs_no_tick_to_run answers for all nine creatures out of one snapshot object.

everyPanelOfTheParty.reading: Уголёк is creature #5, the one the brief measured: 820 entries of which 726 were 'your ration reserve holds', 'enough already', 'somebody in the way' and 'stepped aside'. Its panel used to be four of those. Read bottom to top it is now: it was made whole again at t1995, it came back to work after the wave at t2069, it went to the fourth wave at t2350, and it broke and ran at t2373 on 31% health with four raiders close. Брусок is the one that answers the slice's own question: it broke and ran at t2011, it was whole again at t2271, and at t2384 it would not take the cooking at (14,7) because its nerve had gone at (18,7) at t1703.

theBound.question: Not "how many lines does the panel allow" but "how many beats does one creature's story have".
theBound.answerFromTheQuestion: Four. A creature's party reads as: it went to the wave, the wave cost it something, it came back, and it now refuses the place where that happened. Every one of the nine panels above is exactly that shape.
theBound.answerFromTheBudget: Four. Ten drawn lines at the tightest frame the guard checks; a story sentence runs to about sixty characters and wraps onto two; four sentences plus a header is nine, and Main.AssertLabelsFit refuses five (see evidence/140-mutations.json) and refused six in Issue #128.
whatStaysOffThePanel: the older beats of a story that has more than four kinds — measured 4 to 8 kinds that matter per creature at the end of a baseline party, so between none and four are cut; the newest of each kind is the one kept

every routine decision: waiting on stock, being blocked in a corridor, stepping aside, choosing the next job, and the blow-by-blow of a fight. That is 89 % of a creature's journal — 388 of Брусок's 419 entries
repetitions: a kind a creature took fourteen times shows once, as its newest occurrence. The count is not on the line; the header's third number says how many entries mattered in all
theBound.howItIsSaid: The header carries three numbers — 'STORY · Брусок · 4 of 419 · 31 mattered' — so the panel never claims to be the whole journal. The word 'last' is gone: it was true while the panel was the tail of the journal and would be a lie now, and CreatureStoryTests.The_story_is_bounded_and_the_header_says_what_is_off_the_panel asserts it absent.
theBound.whatWasNotDoneAboutIt: The panel is not made taller and the sentences are not shortened to fit more in. Both would be worth measuring, and both change either the frame guard's arithmetic (Main.cs, held by another task this block) or the wording every other panel shares (EventNarration).

whatThisFoundAndDidNotFix.what: combat_joined is emitted twice with different arguments. 34 of the 48 on this party carry a wave number; the other 14 carry a jobKind and a jobId instead and no wave, so EventNarration prints 'joined the fight for wave ?.'
whatThisFoundAndDidNotFix.whereItShows: That sentence is now often the newest line of a panel, so the gap that used to be buried in a 400-entry journal is on screen.
whatThisFoundAndDidNotFix.whyItIsNotFixedHere: The missing argument is written by the simulation and the sentence lives in EventNarration.cs; this task owns neither and its non-goals name the simulation explicitly. It is a defect the selection surfaced, not one it introduced.
